ing: pierced with a knife; or 1 tbsp lime juice
st: Soak the rinsed rice in cold water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Heat the ghee in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onions for 12 minutes until deep golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, cinnamon, cardamom, baharat and turmeric. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and brown for 8 minutes, then stir in the tomatoes, tomato paste, dried limes and salt.
Pour in [[3.5 cups]] hot water, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Lift out the chicken. Add the drained rice to the broth, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile broil the chicken for 5 minutes to crisp the skin. Rest the rice 5 minutes, fluff, and top with the chicken.
Soak the wheat berries in plenty of cold water overnight (at least 8 hours), then drain.
Put the wheat, chicken, cinnamon stick, cardamom, salt and [[9 cups]] water in a large heavy pot.
Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then cover and simmer on low for 1 hour until the chicken is tender and reaches 165°F (74°C).
Remove the chicken, shred the meat, and discard the bones, skin and spices.
Return the meat to the pot and keep simmering the wheat for 2 hours more, stirring now and then, until it is very soft and the pot looks like porridge.
Add [[2 tbsp]] of the butter and beat the porridge hard with a wooden spoon or masher for 5 minutes until thick and smooth.
Spoon into bowls, make a well in the center, and add the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter, ground cinnamon and sugar if you like.
Heat the ghee in a large pot and brown the lamb in batches for 10 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Cook the onions in the pot for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, baharat and turmeric for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes and tomato paste and cook for 5 minutes.
Return the lamb, add [[6 cups]] water and the salt, and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the potatoes and cook 15 minutes, then add the zucchini and cook 10 more minutes until all is tender.
Toast the bread pieces in a dry skillet or oven until crisp, about 5 minutes, and lay them in a large shallow dish.
Ladle the broth over the bread to soak it, then pile the lamb and vegetables on top. Serve hot.
Melt the butter in a pot over medium heat and fry the vermicelli for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until golden brown.
Pour in [[2 cups]] hot water and add the sugar, cardamom, saffron with its soaking water, and salt.
Cook uncovered for 10 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the noodles are soft but not mushy.
Stir in the rose water if using. Cover and keep warm.
Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt for the omelet.
Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat, pour in the eggs, and cook for 3 minutes until set and golden on both sides. Never leave it raw.
Spoon the noodles onto a plate and top with the omelet, either whole or cut in strips.
In a bowl whisk the flour, cornstarch, yeast, sugar, cardamom and salt together.
Add the saffron with its soaking water and [[1 cup]] warm water. Beat for 3 minutes into a thick, sticky, smooth batter.
Cover and let the batter rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled and bubbly.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C), measured with a thermometer.
Wet a spoon and scoop walnut-sized portions of batter, dropping them into the oil in batches. Do not crowd the pot.
Fry 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Pile onto a plate, drizzle with date syrup and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Serve warm.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a large pot and cook the onion for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, cardamom, turmeric and pepper and stir for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, then add [[7 cups]] water and the salt.
Cover and simmer for 40 minutes until the chicken is falling apart and reaches 165°F (74°C).
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat, and discard the bones.
Add the rice to the broth and cook, stirring often, for 25 minutes until very soft and porridge-like.
Return the chicken to the pot and mash everything with a wooden spoon. Serve topped with the remaining [[1 tbsp]] butter.

ing: or 3 tea bags, strong Assam type
st: Put [[2 cups]] water and the crushed cardamom and ginger in a small pot and bring to a boil.
Add the tea leaves and simmer for 4 minutes until the water is dark and strong.
Pour in the evaporated milk and add the sugar.
Bring back to a gentle boil, watching so it does not boil over, then lower the heat.
Add the saffron and simmer on low for 3 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Strain through a fine sieve into cups.
Taste and add more sugar if you like it sweeter. Serve hot.
